scenario.name: Freedesktop Systemd Spec & Elastic DFIR — Linux systemd Generator (/run/systemd/generator) & Unit Persistence Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a Linux building where every morning janitor inspects the standard wall roster of scheduled jobs, yet overlooks a tiny automated blueprint-printer tucked inside a hidden generator cabinet. An intruder drops an executable blueprint-printer script into that cabinet so every time the building reloads its schedules, the printer invents a brand-new temporary service card on the fly inside volatile memory, leaving the permanent wall roster completely clean until forensic inspectors trace where the temporary card came from. In this scenario (T1543.002, Freedesktop Systemd Spec & Elastic DFIR, Linux systemd Generator (/run/systemd/generator) & Unit Persistence Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: dropping Executable Generator, then ephemeral Unit Synthesis, then forensic Attribution via systemctl. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Dropping Executable Generator, then Ephemeral Unit Synthesis, then Forensic Attribution via systemctl, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 257 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1543.002 - Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service)
stages.description: Holding root access on the Linux server, the intruder drops a tiny executable generator script into the special early-boot generator cabinet that runs automatically before ordinary system services even start. Instead of creating a conspicuous unit file directly in /etc/systemd/system/, the actor drops a small executable script at /etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus- early-check (or /usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/). stages.title: Stage 2: Ephemeral Unit Synthesis in /run/systemd/generator/ on systemctl daemon-reload
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1543.002 - Ephemeral /run/systemd/generator/ Unit Synthesis)
stages.description: Whenever the server boots or an administrator refreshes service configurations, the hidden generator script prints a fresh ephemeral unit card straight into temporary RAM storage and links it onto the multi-user startup rail. When systemctl daemon-reload is triggered, systemd (PID 1) invokes /etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus-early-check, passing /run/systemd/generator as argv[1]. stages.title: Stage 3: Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1543.002 - FragmentPath & journalctl Forensic Attribution)
stages.description: Rather than trusting only the static wall roster, forensic responders inspect every running service exact origin fragment path and audit the generator cabinets directly, immediately exposing the temporary unit and eliminating the root generator script. During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health.service and systemd-analyze unit-paths exposes that the active service originates from /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service, while journalctl _PID=1 correlates the reload timestamp with the generator script (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with UnitName=network-health.service, FragmentPath=/run/systemd/generator/network-health.service , tmpfs, ExecStartBinary=/usr/local/bin/net-telemetry-sync, GeneratorOrigin=/etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus-early-check so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes systemctl show -p Id,FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart,DropInPaths network-health.service (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , systemctl show -p Id,FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart,DropInPaths network-health.service vi so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1543.002 during "Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT" , During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact systemd-analyze verify /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , systemd-analyze verify /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service with its runtime command-line arg so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1543.002 during "Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT" , During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ systemctl show -p FragmentPath,ExecStart network-health.service / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 systemd-generators Directory) to Node ④ (#4 /run/systemd/generator Unit), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 systemd (PID 1) ExecStart).

steps.plainTitle: Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT
steps.storyAnalogy: Rather than trusting only the static wall roster, forensic responders inspect every running service exact origin fragment path and audit the generator cabinets directly, immediately exposing the temporary unit and eliminating the root generator script.
steps.simpleExplanation: During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health.service and systemd-analyze unit-paths exposes that the active service originates from /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service, while journalctl _PID=1 correlates the reload timestamp with the generator script (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with UnitName=network-health.service, FragmentPath=/run/systemd/generator/network-health.service , tmpfs, ExecStartBinary=/usr/local/bin/net-telemetry-sync, GeneratorOrigin=/etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus-early-check so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes systemctl show -p Id,FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart,DropInPaths network-health.service (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , systemctl show -p Id,FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart,DropInPaths network-health.service vi so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1543.002 during "Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT" , During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact systemd-analyze verify /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , systemd-analyze verify /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service with its runtime command-line arg so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1543.002 during "Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT" , During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
